title: feat(govern): send the Codex tool namespace with tool call events
description:
`glab govern audit sync` read only `name` from Codex rollout items, so an MCP tool reached GitLab as a bare name such as `click`, indistinguishable across servers and from built-ins. Codex writes a `namespace` field next to `name`; this sends it, as asked in https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/633374 (question 7).

In 93 real rollouts (Codex CLI 0.118 to 0.159), namespaces were MCP servers (`mcp__computer_use`, `mcp__node_repl`) and app tools (`codex_app`, `collaboration`), sometimes with a trailing separator (`mcp__computer_use__`). Built-in tools never carried one (0 of 4621 `exec_command` items).

## Changes

- Read `namespace` from `function_call` and `custom_tool_call` items.
- `codexToolName` joins them as `<namespace>__<name>` after trimming trailing underscores, so `mcp__computer_use` and `mcp__computer_use__` both give `mcp__computer_use__click`; underscore-only counts as none. Built-ins keep their bare name.
- `toolCall` and `toolResult` carry `Namespace`, copied from call to result.
- `auditEvents` adds `tool_namespace` to `ai_tool_invoked` and result event details when set; agents that record only a name (Cursor, OpenCode) send none.
- API contract unchanged: `details` is free-form and `tool_name` keeps its meaning.

## Example

Rollout item:

```json
{"type":"function_call","name":"click","namespace":"mcp__computer_use","call_id":"call_1"}
```

Event details after (before, `tool_name` was `click`):

```json
{"tool_name": "mcp__computer_use__click", "tool_namespace": "mcp__computer_use", "tool_call_id": "call_1", "agent_initiated": true, "outcome": "pending"}
```

## Alternatives

The qualified name is what Codex gives the model and what other connected agents already report, so the dashboard sees MCP tools consistently and two servers' `click` no longer collide. The raw namespace stays for grouping by server.

Considered keeping `tool_name` bare and adding only `tool_namespace`; rejected because the Top tools card would keep showing ambiguous names like `click`. Open to that shape if you prefer.

The risk card allowlist in https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/261725 keys Codex built-ins (`exec`, `exec_command`, `shell`, `apply_patch`), which never carry a namespace; MCP and app tools stay Unclassified by design.

## Testing

- `TestCodexTranscript_NamespacedToolNames`: built-in, MCP, trailing separator, `custom_tool_call`, separator-only namespace; checks call and result.
- `TestAuditEvents_ToolNamespace`, plus a `NotContains` check in `TestAuditEvents` for agents without one.
- `go test ./internal/commands/govern/...` passes.
- golangci-lint did not run locally (installed binary targets Go 1.24, repo is on 1.27.2); CI is the lint check.

## Out of scope

- Namespaces for other agents.
- Backfilling events already synced.
- Showing the namespace on the dashboard.
